entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Sunil S/o Khetaram, Aged About 27 Years, R/o Riyaan, District Jodhpur
----Petitioners Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Sunil Thanvi S/o Omprakash Thanvi, R/o Shri Industries, Ummedpura, Phalodi, Dist Jodhpur

For Respondent(s) : Mr. Mahipal Bishnoi,
PP JUSTICE DINESH MEHTA Order 18/12/2023 1.

This application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the applicants apprehending their arrest in connection with FIR No.336/2023, registered at Police Station Phalodi, District Jodhpur (Rural) for the offences under Sections 420 & 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the co- accused Smt. Sarla Choudhary has been granted benefit of anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court on 22.08.2023 (S.B.Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 10275/2023 : Smt. Sarla Choudhary Vs. State of Rajasthan) and prayed that the applicants whose case is on identical footing be also granted anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Sarla Choudhary Vs. State of Rajasthan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned Public Prosecutor opposed the applicants' prayer.

[2023:RJ-JD:44280] (2 of 3)
[CRLMB-15696/2023]
4. While deciding the bail application of co-accused Sarla Choudhary, a co-ordinate Bench of this Court has observed thus:-
"4.After going through the FIR and the allegation levelled therein, prima facie, it is revealing that there was a business transaction between the parties, for which as stated in the FIR, the petitioner had given the cheque dated 21.12.2022 of Khetaram vs State Of Rajasthan (2023:Rj-Jd:44280) on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156694905/
1 Rs.15,00,000/- to the complainant.
The submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner seems to be worth considering that there is a fine distinction between a breach of contract and breach of trust.
In light of these facts and circumstances, this Court deems it just and proper to allow the anticipatory bail application.
5.Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

The S.H.O/I.O/Arresting Officer, Police Station Phalodi, District Jodhpur in F.I.R. No.336/2022 is directed that in the event of arrest of the petitioner, she shall be released on bail, provided she furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties in the sum of Rs.25,000/-
each to the satisfaction of the S.H.O/I.O/Arresting Officer of the concerned Police Station on the following conditions:-
(i) that the petitioner shall make herself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii) that the petitioner shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the [2023:RJ-JD:44280] (3 of 3)
[CRLMB-15696/2023] facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer, and (iii) that the petitioner shall not leave India without previous permission of the Court."
5.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and and in order to maintain consistency and parity, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicants.

(DINESH MEHTA),J 227-akansha/-
